options: a:Another name for a four-way intersection.,b:An area designated for road construction workers.,c:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross. It can be marked with painted lines or unmarked at an intersection, but in both cases drivers must watch for pedestrians and yield to them as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not operating, what should you do at the intersection?
options: a:Proceed if the intersection appears clear without stopping.,b:Drive quickly through to avoid blocking traffic.,c:Follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.,d:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way as you would at an all-way stop.
note: When a traffic signal is not working, you must treat the intersection like an all‑way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed only when it is your turn and it is safe, yielding to vehicles and pedestrians who arrived first or are already in the intersection.

question: In a vehicle equipped with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Airbags deploy with great force and can seriously injure children. The safest place for children age 12 and under is the back seat, properly restrained in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt, away from front airbags.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but traffic ahead is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: Having a green light does not give you the right to block an intersection. You must wait behind the stop line until there is enough space on the far side to clear the intersection completely, even if the light is green.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Require the pedestrian to yield to you.,b:Honk to make them aware of your presence.,c:Drive slowly past without stopping.,d:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or partially sighted and using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. You must stop or yield so they can cross safely, and never honk or try to force them to hurry or yield to you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, what is the most likely outcome?
options: a:You will interfere with traffic and could be cited.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving.,d:You will reduce the risk of collisions significantly.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic (when conditions and the speed limit allow faster travel) can block or interfere with other vehicles. This can be unsafe and, in many states, can result in a citation for impeding traffic. Use the right lane and match the flow when it is safe and legal.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,b:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,c:It is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention away from driving. It can occupy your hands (manual distraction), your eyes (visual distraction), and your mind (cognitive distraction), which greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: You are approaching an intersection at speed when the light turns yellow. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to cross before the light turns red.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding to the left, what should you do?
options: a:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,b:Steer to the left.,c:Steer to the right.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go—this is often described as steering into the skid. If the rear of your car skids left, gently steer left to help straighten the vehicle and regain control.

question: If a driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Apply your brakes suddenly to warn them.,c:Reduce your speed gradually to encourage them to pass or change lanes.,d:Maintain speed and refuse to yield.
note: If someone is following too closely, do not speed up or brake suddenly. Gradually slow down to increase your following distance and, when safe, encourage the tailgater to pass or change lanes. This reduces the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,b:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.,c:Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
note: Large trucks have bigger blind spots and need more distance to stop. Stay farther back than you would behind a car so you can see the truck’s mirrors and have enough time to react if it slows or stops suddenly.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: Animals near the road can move suddenly into your path. Slow down, cover the brake, and proceed with caution instead of speeding up or swerving abruptly, which can cause you to lose control or collide with another vehicle.

question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, what should a driver do?
options: a:Have their exhaust system checked regularly to be sure there are no leaks.,b:Keep their engine turned off when their vehicle is enclosed in a garage.,c:Both of the above.
note: Carbon monoxide is a colorless, odorless gas that can quickly become deadly. Prevent poisoning by having your exhaust system checked regularly for leaks and never running the engine in an enclosed area like a closed garage.

question: A driver's license is considered a:
options: a:Right.,b:Requirement.,c:Privilege.,d:Guarantee of safe driving.
note: Driving is not a guaranteed right; it is a privilege granted by the state. You must meet licensing requirements and obey traffic laws, and your license can be suspended or revoked if you violate those laws.

question: When a large truck turns right onto a multi-lane street, what might it need to do?
options: a:Always stay in the right-most lane during the turn.,b:Swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Cut directly across lanes without signaling.,d:Complete the turn in either lane as it chooses.
note: Large trucks have a much wider turning radius and their rear wheels track inside the path of the front wheels. To avoid running over the curb or hitting objects on the right, they often must swing wide to the left before completing a right turn. Drivers behind or beside a truck should never try to squeeze through on the right while it is turning.

question: On interstate highways, drivers are required to:
options: a:Use cruise control at all times.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,d:Both b and c.
note: On interstate highways, traffic typically moves at higher, steady speeds and lane changes and merges happen quickly. Drivers must be able to safely control their vehicle at these higher speeds and remain constantly alert to changing traffic and road conditions. Cruise control is optional, not required, so the correct idea is the need to safely drive at increased speeds, along with staying alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,b:Change lanes without signaling.,c:If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.,d:All of the above are safe practices.
note: On interstates, safe practices include keeping slower traffic to the right and continuing to the next exit if you miss yours. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and usually illegal because other drivers cannot anticipate your movement. You must always signal before changing lanes so traffic around you can adjust safely.

question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Merge into a different lane when possible.,b:Maintain your speed and position no matter what.,c:If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to help them merge.
note: When vehicles are entering a freeway, through traffic should help create a safe gap. If it is safe, move over one lane to give entering drivers more room to merge. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed slightly—either up or down as appropriate—to allow them to enter smoothly without forcing sudden braking or dangerous lane changes.

question: When following a motorcycle, why should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle?
options: a:Because they are easier to see than other vehicles.,b:Because motorcycles can stop quickly and are less visible, so you need more time to react.,c:Because motorcycles always travel below the speed limit.
note: When following a motorcycle, you should leave more following distance than you would for a larger vehicle. Motorcycles can stop more quickly and are less stable and less visible than cars. Extra space gives you more time to react if the rider brakes suddenly, swerves to avoid a hazard, or loses control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Attempt to change lanes within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in the middle of an intersection. Lane changes should be made before or after the intersection, when the path is clear. Before moving over, always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots and make sure no one else is moving into the same lane.

question: Which action tends to block the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Driving at posted speeds.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of driving.,d:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or something on the side of the road (rubbernecking) disrupts the smooth flow of traffic and can cause congestion and additional collisions. Driving at the posted speed when safe, avoiding unnecessary lane changes, and even using public transportation do not block traffic the way rubbernecking does.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill on a hill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight.,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
note: When you park facing downhill, turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge. If the vehicle starts to roll, the front tire will hit the curb or edge and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:Expect the unexpected — children can be unpredictable.,b:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.,c:Beep your horn to alert them.,d:Assume they will always obey traffic rules.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable. They may suddenly swerve, lose balance, or enter the roadway without warning. Expect the unexpected, slow down, and give them extra space instead of assuming they are in full control or will always follow traffic rules.

question: In rainy weather, when is the roadway most slippery?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:If it has been raining all day.
note: The road is usually most slippery during the first few minutes to about the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and other residues on the pavement to form a slick film. As rain continues, this film is washed away and the surface generally becomes less slippery, though you should still drive carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, who must you yield to?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians — you must yield to them.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.,c:You never have to yield when turning left.,d:Only to bicyclists.
note: When turning left, you must wait for a safe gap. Yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians crossing your path in the crosswalk. Only turn when you can complete the turn without forcing others to slow or stop.

question: What is the term for slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual sight and what does it do?
options: a:Sightseeing — it helps emergency responders.,b:Rubbernecking — it causes traffic congestion.,c:Careful observation — it improves traffic flow.,d:Defensive driving — it prevents rear-end collisions.
note: Rubbernecking is when drivers slow down just to look at a crash, stopped vehicle, or other unusual event. This unnecessary slowing disrupts traffic flow, increases congestion, and can cause additional crashes because drivers are not focused on the road ahead.

question: As the percentage of alcohol (BAC) in your blood increases, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More coordinated.,c:More sober.
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the amount of alcohol in your blood. As BAC increases, your judgment, reaction time, and coordination get worse, so you become more impaired and more dangerous behind the wheel.

question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when they are:
options: a:Driving down long, gradual hills.,b:Driving in long, gradual curves.,c:Driving up long or steep hills.,d:Making quick lane changes.
note: Large trucks are heavy and require a lot of power to climb. On long or steep upgrades they slow down, often much more than cars. Give trucks extra space and time when approaching hills, and be prepared for them to move more slowly than other traffic.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol level can lead to license suspension?
options: a:0.08 percent or more.,b:0.15 percent or more.,c:Any measurable amount of alcohol in your system.
note: Alabama enforces a zero-tolerance policy for under-21 drivers; any detectable alcohol can result in license suspension.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean for drivers turning in that direction?
options: a:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.,b:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,c:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. You should prepare to stop if you have not yet entered the intersection, and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Do not speed up to beat the light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Having many passengers in the vehicle.,c:Driving unusually slowly.,d:Keeping a consistent, legal speed.
note: Aggressive drivers often make sudden, unsafe lane changes, follow too closely, and ignore traffic laws. Erratic and improper lane changes are a clear sign of aggressive driving and should alert you to give them space.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, what is the correct action?
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road.,b:Look straight ahead.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare while still letting you use the lane markings and road edge to stay safely in your lane.

question: Prior to entering a curve, what is the correct action?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve so you can steer smoothly and maintain control. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on wet or slippery roads.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often, to observe how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:Only when changing lanes.,d:Every 10 minutes.
note: Frequently checking your mirrors helps you know the positions of nearby vehicles and avoid surprises.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating you have enough space.

question: What does a \No passing zone\" sign indicate?"
options: a:That it is not safe to pass.,b:To speed up slightly.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A No Passing Zone sign marks an area where passing is illegal because conditions make it unsafe to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you use?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, begin from the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the first legal lane in that direction.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Pull over quickly.,c:Hold the steering wheel tightly, ease off the gas, and brake gently when the vehicle is under control.
note: If a tire blows out, the car may pull hard to one side. Grip the steering wheel firmly to keep control and steer straight. Do not slam on the brakes; instead, ease off the accelerator and brake gently only after the vehicle is stable, then move to the side of the road when it is safe.

question: What should you do when taking any medicine with regard to driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.,c:Have someone follow you home.
note: Before driving on any medicine, you should check with your doctor or pharmacist about side effects like drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Some prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can impair driving just like alcohol, so you must know how they affect you before you drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an octagonal sign, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down but proceed if clear.,c:Turn right if possible.,d:Yield only to the vehicle on your right.
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) red sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic before proceeding when it is safe.

question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drug effects from your body?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Give your body time.,c:Breathe in some fresh air.
note: Once alcohol or many drugs are in your system, nothing—coffee, cold showers, fresh air, or exercise—can quickly make you sober. Only time allows your body to metabolize the substance and reduce its impairing effects to safe levels.

question: In very foggy conditions you should slow down and use which lights?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.,c:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can create glare, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them together with low beams to improve visibility.

question: If you must park where parking is not usual, what should you ensure?
options: a:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: If you must park in an unusual or less visible place, make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle from all directions. Use legal parking spots when possible, and avoid creating a hazard or surprise for approaching traffic.

question: Holding a driver license is considered what?
options: a:Requirement.,b:Privilege, not a right.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: A driver license is a privilege granted by the state. You must meet requirements, follow traffic laws, and it can be suspended or revoked. It is not an automatic right.

question: When is it lawful to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When the warning lights are not flashing.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Never.
note: You must never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. Even if you do not see a train, you must wait until the lights stop flashing and the gate is fully raised.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if the vehicle has an outside mirror on each side.,b:Blind spots only exist at low speeds.,c:Blind spots can be checked using the rearview mirror alone.,d:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots on all sides, so you should avoid driving alongside or close behind them where the driver cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to which of the following?
options: a:Passing cars only.,b:Only to vehicles with flashing lights.,c:No one; left-turning vehicles always have priority.,d:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right, and you must also yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing your path.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, and also to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing your path. Only turn when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive quickly to the nearest intersection and stop there.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Pull into the left lane to let it pass.,d:Stay in your lane and slow down but do not stop.
note: On most roads, when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from behind, you must pull as far to the right as safely possible and stop, then remain stopped until it has passed.

question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When the driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,c:When you signal your intention for three seconds.
note: After you pass, you should not move back too soon. Wait until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed (including both headlights) in your inside rearview mirror, then check your blind spot and signal before returning to your lane.

question: When exiting the interstate, when should you begin reducing your speed?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: On interstates, you should stay at highway speed until you reach the deceleration lane. Once you are fully in the deceleration lane, begin slowing to the posted exit or ramp speed so you do not disrupt faster traffic still on the main roadway.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Four-way hazard flashers.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.
note: To avoid dangerous situations, you must be aware of everything happening around your vehicle. Scan ahead, check your mirrors frequently, and watch to the sides so you can spot hazards early and adjust your speed or position in time.

question: Excessive speed increases the likelihood of what outcome?
options: a:Serious bodily injury and death.,b:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,c:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
note: Driving too fast gives you less time to react and makes crashes more severe. Higher speed increases stopping distance and impact force, which greatly raises the chances of serious injury or death if a collision occurs.

question: When you drive through a construction zone, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Pass the construction zone carefully and not 'rubberneck.'
note: In construction zones you should drive through carefully and avoid rubbernecking—slowing or stopping just to watch the work. Rubbernecking increases the risk of rear-end collisions and adds to congestion. Maintain a safe following distance and focus on the road and any work-zone signs or flaggers.

question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what should you do?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Always slow down in your lane.,d:Assume other drivers will yield to you.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see your blind spot—an area your mirrors cannot show—so you don’t move into a lane already occupied by another vehicle.

question: Is it ever allowed to drive while under the influence of medications that impair your driving?
options: a:No — driving while impaired by medication is not allowed.,b:Only if a doctor prescribed them.,c:Only if you do not feel drowsy.,d:Yes, if they are over-the-counter medications.
note: You must not drive if any medication—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—impairs your ability to drive safely. Even if a doctor prescribed it, you are responsible for knowing how it affects you. If it causes drowsiness, slowed reactions, or confusion, you must not drive while under its influence.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Balance.,c:Judgment.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making. You may feel more confident and take risks you normally would avoid, such as speeding or unsafe passing. As you drink more, other abilities like coordination, balance, and vision also become impaired, but poor judgment usually appears first.

question: What are construction zone signs typically like in shape and color?
options: a:Rectangular green signs with white letters.,b:Round signs with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square signs with white and red coloring.,d:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black symbols.
note: Construction and work-zone signs are usually diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black letters or symbols. The bright orange color warns you to slow down, watch for workers and equipment, and be prepared for lane shifts or other changes in normal traffic patterns.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.,c:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
note: When your vehicle hydroplanes, the tires are riding on water instead of the road, so any sudden braking or steering can cause a complete loss of control. Ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and slow down gradually without hard braking until the tires regain contact with the road.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what braking action should you take?
options: a:Brake abruptly.,b:Brake lightly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: In most skids, especially on slippery roads, you should stay off the brakes and focus on steering in the direction you want the front of the car to go. Braking hard can lock the wheels and make the skid worse. Once the vehicle begins to straighten out and you have more control, you can brake gently if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and force other vehicles to move.,b:Check traffic behind and beside you, then watch the vehicle ahead in the gap.,c:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
note: When entering a gap in highway traffic, you must be aware of vehicles all around you. Check your mirrors and blind spots for vehicles behind and to the side, then focus on the vehicle ahead in the gap you plan to enter so you can match speed and merge smoothly without cutting anyone off.

question: How can you reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Drive at the posted speed regardless of conditions.,c:Make abrupt turns to test traction.,d:Slow down.
note: On wet roads, the best way to reduce the chance of losing traction or hydroplaning is to slow down. Lower speed allows your tires more time to push water aside and maintain contact with the road. Avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and make sure your tires are in good condition.

question: As a driver, what areas around your vehicle should you monitor?
options: a:Stare directly in front of the car at all times.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Only check the mirrors once per mile.,d:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of your vehicle.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan all around their vehicle. You should look well ahead to see what is coming, check beside you to know what is in adjacent lanes, and use your mirrors to monitor traffic behind. This all-around awareness helps you spot hazards early and react in time.

question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, what is required?
options: a:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,b:Slow down to a maximum of 10 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Change lanes and pass slowly.,d:Proceed if you are on a different street.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm out, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. Passing is illegal and extremely dangerous because children may be crossing the road.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,c:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
note: You should leave extra space behind large vehicles like trucks and buses because they block your view of the road ahead and have large blind spots. A greater following distance lets you see traffic conditions sooner and helps keep you out of the truck’s blind spots, giving you more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,b:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.,c:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.
note: At railroad crossings, trains always have the right-of-way. You must obey all warning devices and directions: if a flagger, stop sign, or flashing lights indicate you must stop, you are required to stop and not proceed until it is clearly safe and legal to do so.

question: How can drowsiness affect your driving?
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Help you to be a better driver.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness makes you a dangerous driver. It slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and impairs your judgment in ways similar to alcohol or drugs. You may not notice hazards in time or may make poor decisions, greatly increasing your crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians in the crosswalk and no one else.,b:Only oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.,c:All approaching vehicles and pedestrians who are in or about to enter the crosswalk.,d:Only vehicles that are speeding.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. You may only turn when it is safe and you will not interfere with approaching vehicles. This means you yield to all approaching vehicles that have the right-of-way, not just those also turning left.

question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,b:Stay within that speed range.,c:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.
note: Traveling at about the same speed as surrounding traffic, while staying within the posted speed limit, is safest. Large speed differences—either faster or slower than the flow—create more lane changes and conflicts, which increases crash risk.

question: How can you keep aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: You should check your mirrors frequently so you know what is happening behind you and can react early to vehicles that are following too closely or moving quickly. Combine mirror checks with occasional quick glances over your shoulder when changing lanes to cover blind spots.

question: Before driving, from which vehicle surfaces should you remove snow, frost, and ice?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:Just the windshield and passenger window.,c:All windows and other necessary surfaces such as mirrors and lights.
note: Clear all windows and mirrors so you have full visibility before driving.

question: If you observe heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.,b:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.,d:Continue at normal speed but use your horn to warn others.
note: When smoke or fog is so heavy that you cannot see the road ahead, slow down, move as far right as you safely can, and stop completely off the roadway. Keep your low-beam headlights and hazard flashers on so others can see you, and wait until visibility improves before continuing.

question: When must vehicles stopped behind a school bus remain stopped?
options: a:The stop arm is retracted.,b:All students are off the bus.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, traffic in most situations must stop in both directions. Stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing, the stop arm is retracted, and the bus begins moving again, ensuring children are safely clear of the roadway.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Use the brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, stay off the brakes at first, and let the car slow by easing off the accelerator. Once the vehicle is under control and slowing, use the brakes lightly and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: Tailgating (driving too closely to another vehicle's bumper) can do what?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Can result in a traffic citation.,c:Increases the risk of a rear-end collision.
note: Following too closely is dangerous and discourteous. Tailgating can anger or frighten other drivers, increase the chance of a rear‑end crash, and can result in a traffic citation. Always leave enough following distance so you can stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows or stops.

question: When an oncoming car has very bright headlights at night, how should you react?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. Do not look directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road to use it as a guide, while still checking the road ahead frequently until the vehicle passes.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only when making a permitted left turn or when instructed by traffic control or emergency personnel.

question: What does a steady green traffic signal allow approaching drivers to do?
options: a:Increase their speed to quickly clear the intersection.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Continue through the intersection or make permitted turns when the way is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or make any turn that is not prohibited by signs or signals, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What is the crash risk effect of a BAC of 0.02 percent?
options: a:Won't put other drivers at risk.,b:Will increase your chances of having an accident.,c:Won't have any effect on your driving.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol (around 0.02% BAC) can measurably affect judgment, attention, and reaction time, which increases crash risk compared with sober driving. However, it does not reliably double the crash risk; the risk roughly doubles closer to 0.05% BAC. The key idea is that there is no completely safe BAC above zero—any alcohol can increase your chances of a crash.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk.,b:To pedestrians in any marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection.,c:Only to pedestrians crossing at mid-block locations.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. An unmarked crosswalk exists at most intersections, even if there are no painted lines. You should also be prepared to yield to pedestrians crossing the street in other places when it is necessary to avoid a collision.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,c:At all times.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and stop for them when necessary; yield to anyone already in the intersection or crosswalk.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Many drugs can impair driving, including legal prescription medications and over‑the‑counter medicines such as some cold, allergy, or sleep aids. They can slow your reactions, affect judgment, or make you drowsy. It is illegal and unsafe to drive when impaired by any drug, not just illegal ones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,b:Often, even at controlled intersections.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.
note: Having the legal right-of-way never guarantees that others will yield. You should be willing to give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent a collision. Defensive drivers focus on avoiding crashes, not on insisting on their legal priority.

question: Traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas are normally what color?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Yellow.
note: In work zones, traffic control devices such as signs, cones, drums, and barriers are typically orange. This color alerts drivers that they are entering a construction or maintenance area and should slow down and use extra caution.

question: If a road is slippery, how should your following distance change?
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c:Closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and it takes longer to stop. You should increase your following distance so you have more time and space to brake gently and avoid skidding if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: When driving in fog what lighting and speed practices are recommended?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Reduce your speed so you have time to react to hazards, and if visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait until conditions improve.

question: What does a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line mean regarding passing?
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line. Drivers on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass, because it indicates that passing from that side is unsafe.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic in your blind spot?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, you must quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots, in addition to using your mirrors and signal.

question: What can happen if a driver leaves a gas station without paying for gas?
options: a:Have their license suspended.,b:Be given a warning.,c:Not face any consequences.
note: Leaving a gas station without paying is treated as theft. In many states, including Alabama, a conviction can lead to criminal penalties and license suspension, because using a vehicle to commit theft is considered a serious offense.

question: To be able to turn quickly and safely, where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Keeping your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel (commonly around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions) gives you the best control and allows you to turn quickly and smoothly while maintaining stability of the vehicle.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the safest action?
options: a:Switch your lights to high beams.,b:Turn your lights on and off.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road.
note: When oncoming headlights are too bright, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This helps you avoid being blinded while still keeping your vehicle in the correct position on the road.

question: What do yellow lines on the roadway separate?
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.,c:Bicycle lanes from vehicle lanes.,d:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. They mark the center of the roadway and help drivers stay on the correct side of the road.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Leave the front wheels straight.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Ignore the officer and obey the light.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,d:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions override traffic lights and signs. If an officer clearly directs you to proceed through a red light, you must follow the officer’s directions, moving carefully through the intersection while watching for other road users.

question: When entering the interstate, after finding a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Merge carefully into the gap.,b:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.,c:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.
note: On an interstate entrance ramp, you should use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, and then merge carefully into a safe gap. Other drivers are not required to yield to you; it is your responsibility to adjust speed and position so you can merge smoothly without forcing others to brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on the interstate?
options: a:70 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:80 mph.
note: In Alabama, the general statutory speed limit on interstate highways is 70 mph unless signs show a different limit. Always follow posted speed limit signs, as some stretches may be lower due to urban areas, construction zones, or special conditions.

question: When backing up your vehicle, what is the proper way to look?
options: a:Look through the rear window.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Press hard on the gas pedal.
note: When backing up, turn your body and look directly through the rear window so you can clearly see what is behind you. Use your mirrors as helpers, but do not rely on them alone, and back up slowly so you can stop immediately if something enters your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curbside parking spot, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Honk before entering to warn other drivers.,d:Wait for a large enough gap so you can accelerate to the speed of traffic.
note: When pulling out from a curb, you must wait for a gap in traffic that is large enough for you to signal, pull out, and accelerate to the speed of other vehicles without making them slow or swerve. Entering too soon or relying on your horn is unsafe; matching the flow of traffic smoothly is the goal.

question: When a pedestrian guided by a dog or with a white cane is crossing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian.,b:Only yield if you are at a marked crosswalk.,c:Tell them where it is safe to cross.,d:Proceed if they are not in your lane.
note: Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired and using a white cane or guide dog. This applies whether or not they are in a marked crosswalk. Slow or stop early and allow them to cross safely.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do to alert others?
options: a:Signal and move into the slow lane and continue driving.,b:Turn off your lights to conserve battery.,c:Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.,d:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as it's safe.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, you should signal, move off the roadway to a safe place as soon as possible, and turn on your hazard lights. This warns other drivers that your vehicle is disabled and reduces the risk of a collision.

question: If you intend to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assuming signaling guarantees a safe pass.,b:Assuming the other driver will make space for you to return to the lane.,c:Assuming the road ahead is clear.,d:Assuming the other driver will maintain a constant speed.
note: When passing, never assume other drivers will create space for you to return to your lane. You are responsible for making sure there is enough clear distance ahead, that the lane is open, and that you can safely move back without forcing others to slow or swerve.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street, how should you respond?
options: a:Do not have to stop for them.,b:Must stop or slow as needed to avoid hitting them.,c:Should honk your horn at them.
note: Even if pedestrians are crossing illegally (jaywalking), you must do whatever is necessary to avoid hitting them. The law requires drivers to exercise due care to protect pedestrians, so slow down or stop if needed and pass only when it is clearly safe.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when a crossing guard is present.,b:At all times — they always have the right-of-way.,c:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,d:Only at marked crosswalks.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired and using a white cane or guide dog have special legal protection. You must always yield to them, stop well back, and never honk or try to direct them. This applies at all crossings and driveways, marked or unmarked.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the edge of the pavement, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gently. Sudden braking or jerking the wheel back onto the road can cause you to lose control or skid into oncoming traffic. Once you’ve slowed and checked that traffic is clear, steer smoothly back onto the pavement.

question: What should you check before bringing your vehicle to a stop at a traffic signal or sign?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Press down hard on the accelerator.,c:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
note: Before stopping at a signal or sign, check your mirrors so you know what traffic is doing behind and beside you. This helps you brake smoothly and gives you time to react if a driver behind is not slowing down. Then apply your brakes gradually to come to a safe, controlled stop.

question: If you are involved in a collision, how should you treat injured people?
options: a:Avoid moving the injured unless absolutely necessary.,b:Move the injured to their desired location.,c:Insist the injured are fine without immediate medical attention.
note: After a collision, do not move injured people unless there is an immediate danger such as fire, risk of explosion, or another vehicle about to hit. Moving someone with a neck, back, or internal injury can make the injury worse. Keep them still, calm, and warm, and call 911 for medical help.

question: How should you drive on a dimly lit street at night?
options: a:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.,b:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
note: On a dimly lit street at night, drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called not overdriving your headlights. If something appears in your lane, you need enough visible distance to brake and stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the statutory speed limit on a country paved road?
options: a:55 mph.,b:30 mph.,c:20 mph.,d:Varies by state; obey posted signs and your state’s default rural speed limit.
note: Statutory speed limits on rural or country roads vary by state; many states use 55 mph or higher on rural paved roads, while others use 45 mph or different values. Because there is no single nationwide statutory speed for a “country paved road,” you must always follow the posted speed limit and, if no sign is present, obey your own state’s default speed law for that type of road.

question: If you plan to pass a pedestrian while an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to make the pedestrian move over.,b:Quickly swerve into the shoulder to pass.,c:Keep your speed steady because the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,d:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
note: When you face both an oncoming vehicle and a pedestrian in your lane, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first so you only deal with one hazard at a time. Once the oncoming vehicle has gone by and the lane is clear, you can safely move around the pedestrian with plenty of space.

question: When is it necessary to use your low beam headlights?
options: a:On a freeway.,b:In fog.,c:On a lighted street.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, you should use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off moisture in the air and can shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams give you better visibility and make it easier for other drivers to see you without creating glare.

question: You are approaching a steady yellow traffic signal and have not entered the intersection. What should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you are expected to slow down and stop if you can do so safely. Only continue through if you are too close to the intersection to stop without braking hard or creating a hazard for drivers behind you.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle approaching with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or a siren, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right edge or curb of the road and come to a complete stop, remaining stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to re-enter traffic.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what may they do legally?
options: a:They may cut through all lanes at once.,b:They may use the left lane.,c:They must dismount and walk their bike.,d:They must always stay to the right.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of vehicles. When making a left turn, a bicyclist may legally move into and use the left turn lane or left lane, just like a car. Expect to see bicycles in the left part of the lane when they are preparing for or completing a left turn.

question: How far should you follow a large truck on the freeway compared to a passenger vehicle?
options: a:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.,b:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.,c:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.
note: Large trucks block more of your view and need more distance to stop, so you should follow them at a greater distance than you would a passenger car. Leaving extra space gives you a better view of the road ahead and more time to react if the truck slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful?
options: a:Passing another vehicle in a marked no-passing zone.,b:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,c:Both of the above.,d:Passing on a two-lane road when the vehicle ahead signals a left turn.
note: Passing in a marked no‑passing zone or while going over a railroad crossing is illegal because your view of oncoming traffic and potential hazards is limited. You must never pass in these situations. Passing a vehicle that is turning left can be legal when done safely and where not otherwise prohibited.

question: To help prevent eye fatigue when driving at night, you should:
options: a:Continue moving your eyes and scanning the road.,b:Stare straight ahead.,c:Rest your eyes by closing them for a couple of seconds at a time.
note: To reduce eye fatigue at night, keep your eyes moving: scan from side to side and near to far instead of staring straight ahead. This helps you notice hazards sooner and prevents your eyes from becoming tired or fixed on one spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you come to an intersection and your view to the side is blocked, what should you do?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Maintain your speed and look both ways.
note: When your view at an intersection is blocked, you must stop first, then slowly move forward until you can clearly see cross traffic. Only proceed when you are sure the way is clear. This prevents you from pulling into the path of vehicles you could not see at first.

question: Which statement about driving while taking medications is correct?
options: a:Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.,b:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,c:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
note: Many cold and allergy medications can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, and affect judgment, even when taken as directed. Always read labels and talk with your doctor or pharmacist before driving while on any medication.

question: Which best describes how a defensive driver thinks?
options: a:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,b:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road and think ahead about what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do. By anticipating mistakes and being ready to react safely, they reduce the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which circumstances?
options: a:You must stop only at marked stop signs.,b:You must stop only where there is a red traffic light.,c:You must stop only if a police officer orders it and no lights are present.,d:You must stop when a police officer orders you to stop and when traffic controls such as red lights or stop signs require a stop.
note: You must always obey a police officer’s directions, even if traffic signals or signs say something different. You are also required to stop at red traffic lights (steady or flashing) and at stop signs, because these controls are used to keep traffic moving safely and prevent crashes.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can often stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to brake safely if the motorcycle stops suddenly, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Which statement about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are eliminated by one outside mirror.,c:Blind spots can be checked using only the rearview mirror.,d:Blind spots disappear at highway speeds.
note: All vehicles have blind spots—areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars, so you should avoid lingering alongside or close behind them where the driver may not see you.

question: What is a potential effect of taking a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can interact with alcohol to slow your reactions, affect judgment, and make you drowsy. This combination can make you unsafe and legally unfit to drive.

question: When driving through a construction zone, what should you expect?
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones often have changing traffic patterns, workers close to moving vehicles, and equipment entering the roadway. You should expect unexpected hazards, reduce speed, and drive with extra caution to protect workers and yourself.

question: If you want to enter the freeway but there is no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Adjust your speed on the ramp to wait for or create a safe gap.,b:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, you should adjust your speed so you can merge smoothly into a safe gap in traffic. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary, because it is difficult and unsafe to accelerate from a stop into fast‑moving traffic. Instead, slow or slightly adjust your speed on the ramp so you can merge safely.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,b:Allowed from both directions.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only when making a permitted left turn or when turning into or out of a driveway or side road, not to pass another vehicle.

question: When you encounter orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what is required?
options: a:Change lanes immediately and maintain your speed.,b:Ignore the signs if traffic is light.,c:Speed up to clear the zone quickly.,d:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and reduce your speed.
note: Orange signs and cones indicate a work zone. You must slow down, be prepared for lane shifts, stopped or slow traffic, and workers or equipment near the roadway. Follow posted work‑zone speed limits and be ready to stop if necessary.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to the curb, but not away from it.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Use your turn signal any time you change your position on the road, including when pulling toward a curb to park and when leaving the curb to reenter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your movement and react safely.

question: At a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Be alert for vehicles that must stop at all crossings and for multiple trains.,b:Proceed quickly if you don't see a train.,c:Only watch for trains in one direction.,d:Ignore stopped vehicles in the area.
note: At railroad crossings, you must slow down, look, and listen for trains in both directions and be prepared to stop. Some vehicles, like school buses and hazardous materials trucks, are required to stop at all crossings, so you should be alert for them as well. Never try to beat a train; trains are much faster and take far longer to stop than cars.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:Are being tailgated by another driver.,c:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,d:In bad weather, poor visibility, or other higher‑risk conditions.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions increase risk, such as when you are being tailgated, driving in poor weather, following large vehicles, or when visibility is reduced. If someone is tailgating you, leaving extra space in front gives you more room to slow or stop gradually, reducing the chance of a rear-end collision.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You must stay within your lane.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so. Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.

question: You want to turn right but see a pedestrian with a guide dog at the corner ready to cross. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the person crosses the street.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,c:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or canes have the right-of-way; wait for them to complete crossing before turning.

question: What must approaching drivers do when they see a red traffic signal?
options: a:Continue driving through the intersection without stopping.,b:Increase their speed to quickly clear the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: At a steady red traffic signal, you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk, stop line, or entering the intersection. Remain stopped until the light turns green or you are allowed to make a legal turn on red after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

question: If you see pedestrians near the road, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: When pedestrians are near the road, you must slow down, be ready to stop, and pass with extra caution. Reducing speed gives you more time to react if someone suddenly steps into your lane.

question: If you see a lane sign showing an arrow with the word ONLY beneath it above your lane, what does it mean?
options: a:You must proceed only in the direction shown by the arrow.,b:You should always change lanes immediately.,c:Follow the destination signs rather than the arrow.,d:The sign is advisory and can be ignored.
note: A lane sign with an arrow and the word ONLY means that if you stay in that lane, you must go in the direction of the arrow and no other. You should be in the correct lane before reaching the sign so you can follow the required direction safely.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means what?
options: a:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.,c:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to go in the direction of the arrow. You must wait until the arrow turns green (or is replaced by a signal that allows movement) before making that turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:When traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left.,b:When you increase your speed before the turn.,c:When traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the right.
note: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if traffic on the street you are turning onto flows to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Make the turn from the left lane into the left lane of the new street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what speed should you try to achieve?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near the speed of traffic already on the freeway, as long as it is safe and within the speed limit. Matching the flow of traffic makes merging smoother and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: If you come to a railroad crossing with gates lowered and flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted.,b:Drive around the gates if no train is visible.,c:Slow down and proceed carefully past the gates.,d:Stop on the tracks to check both directions.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop well before the gate and remain stopped until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing. Driving around the gates or stopping on the tracks is illegal and extremely dangerous because trains cannot stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:All of the above.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must signal to let others know your intentions and check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure the lane is clear. Doing all of these steps helps prevent collisions with vehicles you may not see in your mirrors alone.

question: If you park uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them to the right (toward the side of the road) so the vehicle would roll away from the center.,b:Leave them straight ahead.,c:Turn them left toward the center of the road.,d:Turn them toward the nearest driveway.
note: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the side of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic, reducing the risk of a collision.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:So others can see your vehicle.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:To warn others of bad weather conditions.
note: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, headlights help other drivers see your vehicle and judge its distance and speed. In many states, including Alabama, you must use low-beam headlights whenever your windshield wipers are on or visibility is reduced.

question: Why is it important to look far ahead while driving on a highway?
options: a:It reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Helps you keep up with traffic.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Looking far ahead on the highway lets you spot slow traffic, hazards, and lane closures early. This gives you time to adjust speed or change lanes smoothly, reducing sudden braking or swerving and helping traffic flow more safely.

question: Accruing how many points on your license within two years will result in a one-year suspension?
options: a:24 or more,b:21 to 23,c:18 to 20
note: Under Alabama’s point system, accumulating 24 or more points within a two‑year period can result in a one‑year (365‑day) license suspension. Lower point totals can also lead to suspensions, but for shorter periods.

question: If you are about to be rear-ended, which action should you NOT take?
options: a:Press your head against the head restraint.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Release your seat belt.
note: In a rear‑end collision, you should keep your seat belt fastened, press your head firmly against the head restraint, and brace yourself. The seat belt and head restraint work together to reduce the risk of whiplash and serious injury. Never release your seat belt when a crash is imminent.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of what?
options: a:Driving more carefully.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Missing an exit only.,d:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Driving while fatigued greatly increases your risk of dozing off or falling asleep at the wheel. Fatigue slows reaction time, impairs judgment, and can lead to drifting out of your lane or crashing, including falling asleep behind the wheel.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or at an equipment check, what must a driver produce?
options: a:Only their license.,b:Only their insurance and registration.,c:Their license, insurance, and registration.
note: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must be able to show your driver’s license, proof of vehicle registration, and proof of insurance. These documents show that you are legally allowed to drive and that the vehicle is properly registered and insured.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not enter an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red. When is it acceptable to enter in this situation?
options: a:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,b:Under any circumstances.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: You must not enter an intersection if traffic ahead will force you to stop and block the intersection, even if the light is green. Only enter when you are sure you can completely clear the intersection without stopping in it; blocking cross traffic is illegal and unsafe.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even when no crosswalk is present; stop and allow them to finish crossing safely.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams while driving at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Flash your high beams to remind them to dim theirs.,d:Close your eyes briefly until the vehicle passes.
note: Bright headlights can temporarily blind you if you look directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to track the oncoming vehicle while maintaining your lane position and speed as safely as possible.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly than usual.,b:Be ready to use your horn often.,c:Follow at the same distance as you would a car.,d:Allow a larger following distance (3–4 seconds).
note: Motorcycles are smaller, can stop quickly, and may be less stable than cars. Leave a larger following distance—at least 3–4 seconds—so you have extra time and space to react if the motorcycle slows or stops suddenly.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Turn your front wheels parallel to the road regardless of curb presence.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear).,c:Leave the car in neutral if you expect to return soon.,d:One of your rear wheels must touch the curb.
note: On any hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (automatic) or in gear (manual). This helps prevent the vehicle from rolling if the primary brakes fail; you then turn the wheels appropriately based on whether there is a curb and which way the vehicle would roll.

question: As you approach the crest of a hill, you should:
options: a:Speed up slightly to maintain momentum.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary and reduce speed as needed.,c:Maintain a steady speed regardless of visibility.,d:Move to the left side of the lane for a better view.
note: When you approach the top of a hill, your view of what’s ahead is limited. Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop in case there is a stopped vehicle, pedestrian, animal, or other hazard just over the crest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to take when making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Always move to the left lane.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Before turning, you must check traffic in all directions—ahead, behind, and to the sides—to be sure the turn can be made safely. This includes checking mirrors and blind spots and adjusting your speed as needed.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Try to fight it.,b:Take a break.,c:Take some caffeine pills.
note: If you feel drowsy, stop at the nearest safe place to rest, nap, stretch, or switch drivers; caffeine is not a safe substitute for rest.

question: How must you yield right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,c:Stop immediately, even if you are within an intersection.
