note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and flashing lights, you must pull as close as you safely can to the right edge of the road and stop, then remain stopped until it has passed. Do not stop in an intersection; if you are in one, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: If you are involved in a minor collision with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: In a minor collision with no injuries and drivable vehicles, you should move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so. Moving to the shoulder or a nearby safe area helps prevent additional crashes and keeps traffic flowing.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what is still required for best protection?
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn.,b:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,c:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. For the best protection, always wear your lap and shoulder belt properly, even in vehicles equipped with airbags.

question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what is the correct braking action?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, braking can make the skid worse by locking the wheels and reducing your ability to steer. The safest action is usually to stay off the brakes and focus on steering smoothly in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go until you regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left, pass on the shoulder.,b:Only if the shoulder is wide enough.,c:If traffic is stopped, pass on the shoulder.,d:No — do not drive on the shoulder to pass.
note: You must not drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is for emergencies and breakdowns, not for travel or passing. Other drivers may pull onto the shoulder unexpectedly, so using it as a passing lane is dangerous and illegal in most situations.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to stay safe?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra room to see hazards and stop safely. Use high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic; never stare directly into other vehicles’ headlights.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield to anyone with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: After passing a large truck, how should you re-enter the lane?
options: a:Give the truck plenty of room before you move back into the lane.,b:Re-enter immediately and then slow down.,c:Re-enter whenever you feel like it.,d:Cut in front quickly to prevent the truck from speeding up.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and have bigger blind spots. After passing, do not move back into the lane until you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have left enough space and reduces the risk of being rear-ended if you need to slow down.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.,b:Continue driving, but try to stay out of its way.,c:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights and a siren, you must pull as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and come to a complete stop. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely. Do not speed up, block the lane, or try to outrun the vehicle.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Maintaining a steady speed.,b:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early helps drivers behind you judge distance and react smoothly, which encourages them to maintain a safe following distance. Sudden speeding up or slowing down can cause tailgating or rear-end collisions.

question: Which habits are dangerous when driving through work zones?
options: a:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers/equipment.,b:Only tailgating other vehicles.,c:Only failing to watch for workers and equipment.,d:Driving at posted speed limits.
note: Work zones require extra caution. Following too closely (tailgating) gives you little time to react to sudden stops, and not watching for workers, equipment, and lane shifts greatly increases crash risk. You should slow down, increase following distance, and stay alert for workers and machinery.

question: A broken yellow centerline between lanes indicates:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,d:Traffic flows in the same direction on both sides of the line.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing on the left is allowed when the lane is clear of oncoming traffic. You must be sure you have enough space and visibility to pass safely before crossing the line.

question: At an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe to do so.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You must slow down, scan for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and then continue through the intersection only when it is safe. Unlike a flashing red light, you are not required to stop first.

question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to do what?
options: a:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,b:Inconvenience drivers.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
note: Work zone devices mark hazardous areas and direct traffic to protect both workers and road users; obey them and slow down.

question: Which action is appropriate when driving at night?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance in the dark to allow more time to respond; use high beams appropriately and avoid staring at oncoming lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after stopping?
options: a:You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,b:You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.,c:You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: After a full stop, turning left on red is only allowed from a one-way street onto another one-way street unless prohibited by signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed repeatedly on both sides while in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.,d:Increase speed to stay out of others' way.
note: On multi-lane roads, drive in the right lane unless passing or preparing for a left turn; use right lanes if traveling slower than traffic flow.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Stop only if you are behind the bus.,b:Slowly pass the bus while watching for children.,c:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are in sight.,d:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and lights stop flashing.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing lights and extended stop arm until the bus moves and the signals are turned off.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:They require longer distances to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They have air brakes that always allow rapid stops.,c:They are more maneuverable than cars.,d:They stop in the same distance as passenger cars.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger vehicles, so even with good brakes they need more distance to stop at the same speed. You should never assume a truck can stop as quickly as a car; leave extra space in front of and behind large trucks.

question: Which of the following is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,b:Using high beam headlights in fog.,c:Staring fixedly at the road ahead with no scanning.,d:Driving with only parking lights at night.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the road and check mirrors every few seconds to stay aware of traffic behind and beside them. In fog you should use low beams, not high beams, and you must always use your regular headlights at night, not just parking lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate from a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match the flow of traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.
note: If there is no acceleration lane, you must judge traffic carefully, wait for a safe gap, and then accelerate firmly to match the speed of traffic as you merge. Never use the shoulder as a makeshift acceleration lane, and do not force your way in without a safe opening.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low beam headlights because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Fog lights may be used in addition to low beams if your vehicle has them, but they do not replace low beams.

question: The measurement of alcohol in a person's blood is known as:
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,d:Breath alcohol index (BAI).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the standard measure of how much alcohol is in a person’s bloodstream, usually expressed as a percentage. Higher BAC levels mean greater impairment and increased risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: At a Yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let any traffic, bicyclists, or pedestrians that are close enough to be a hazard go first. Only enter or cross when you are sure you can do so without forcing others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light when you approach it?
options: a:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,b:May not proceed until it changes to green.,c:You are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:No one.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:Overtaking cars.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, as well as to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Turn only when there is a safe gap so you do not interfere with oncoming vehicles.

question: Which statement about roadwork zones is true?
options: a:Fines are the same for violations committed in work zones as they are under normal traffic conditions.,b:You must 'Slow for the Cone Zone.'.,c:Slow down only if you think workers are present.
note: In work zones, you must slow down, obey all posted work‑zone signs, and be prepared for workers, equipment, and sudden changes in traffic patterns. Many states increase fines for violations in work zones to improve safety for workers and drivers.

question: What is the only factor that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat,b:Drinking caffeine,c:Time
note: Only time lowers your BAC. Your body needs time to metabolize alcohol; food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not speed up this process or make you sober more quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.,b:Quickly turn in front of the truck to avoid delay.,c:Squeeze between the vehicle and the curb to turn.,d:Sound your horn and pass on the right.
note: Large trucks and buses need extra space to turn and often swing wide. Never try to squeeze between a turning large vehicle and the curb or cut in front of it. Stay back and wait until the truck or bus has fully completed its turn before you make your right turn.

question: In bad weather, what steering and braking technique should you use?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly.,b:Steer off the road in all bad weather conditions.,c:Drive in a low gear on all roads in bad weather.
note: In rain, snow, ice, or other bad weather, you are more likely to skid if you make sudden steering or braking movements. Steer and brake gently and smoothly so your tires maintain traction and you keep control of the vehicle.

question: Excessive speed often results in:
options: a:Higher crash risk and more severe collisions.,b:Increased ability to react to a hazard.,c:No change in crash risk.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to see hazards and make safe decisions. At higher speeds, you are more likely to misjudge distances, react late, and choose risky maneuvers, and any crash will be more severe.

question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what is permitted?
options: a:You may cross the line to pass or change lanes when it is safe.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass or change lanes.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so. Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn or when specifically allowed by signs.

question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line between lanes means two-way traffic with passing allowed in both directions when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe. Always check for sufficient space and visibility before crossing the center line.

question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should be your first response?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: When a vehicle cuts in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator to increase following distance smoothly. Avoid sudden braking or swerving, which can cause a rear-end collision or loss of control.

question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line indicate for the side with the broken line?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:Vehicles on both sides may pass anytime.,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,d:No passing allowed for either side.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means the side with the broken line may pass when it is safe, while the side with the solid line may not pass. Always ensure there is enough clear distance and no oncoming traffic before passing.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, tire traction is reduced, so you must slow down below the posted speed and drive smoothly. Gentle steering, braking, and acceleration help maintain control and reduce the risk of skidding.

question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Stop, proceeding only when all the pedestrians have crossed.,c:Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: If a driver stops at a crosswalk, you must also stop and not pass the stopped vehicle. Pedestrians may be crossing in front of that vehicle and hidden from your view. Proceed only after all pedestrians have completely crossed and the crosswalk is clear.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Warning.,b:Yield.,c:Stop.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings, and are usually yellow or orange.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you must stop on snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System), you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it. The system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup, allowing you to steer while braking hard on slippery surfaces.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as what?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is classified as a depressant. It slows brain and nervous system activity, reducing judgment, coordination, and reaction time, which makes driving unsafe even at low levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a turn lane to prepare for a left turn where there is oncoming traffic, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Move to the left of the center lane and stop.,b:Turn your front wheels left to be ready to turn.,c:Honk to warn oncoming traffic.,d:Signal well in advance and keep your front wheels pointed straight until you begin the turn.
note: When preparing for a left turn from a turn lane, signal well in advance and keep your front wheels pointed straight until you actually start turning. If you are hit from behind while your wheels are turned, your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: Your vehicle may hydroplane at speeds as low as approximately:
options: a:25 miles per hour.,b:45 miles per hour.,c:40 miles per hour.,d:35 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can start at about 35 mph when there is enough water on the road for your tires to ride on top of it instead of gripping the surface. Slowing down in wet conditions helps maintain traction and steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always drive at what speed?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,c:At the speed limit.
note: You must always choose a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions, even if that means driving below the posted speed limit. Never exceed the speed limit, and slow down when visibility, road surface, or traffic conditions are poor.

question: When should you allow an extra cushion of space around your vehicle?
options: a:When following a small passenger car.,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c:When following a station wagon.
note: Leave extra following distance behind large vehicles such as trucks, buses, and vehicles towing trailers because they have large blind spots and may block your view of the road ahead. More space gives you extra time to react if they stop or slow suddenly.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, what should you try to do?
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Stop in the right lane.,c:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled, you should, if possible, move completely off the traveled portion of the highway so you are not in the path of moving traffic. Parking with all four wheels off the roadway greatly reduces the risk of a collision.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean for turning in that direction?
options: a:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,b:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped; you may not turn in the direction of the arrow until a green arrow or green light allows the movement, unless a specific state law and sign allow a turn on red. Treat it like a red light for that direction of travel.

question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Brake hard before entering the puddle.,b:Maintain the posted speed to drive through it.,c:Shift into neutral as you go through the water.,d:Avoid the puddle if possible.
note: Deep or large puddles can cause hydroplaning, loss of control, or mechanical damage. If you can safely do so, steer around the puddle or choose another path so your tires stay on a more predictable, dry surface.

question: When near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid?
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. If you drive beside them for a long time, the driver may not see you and you have less room to react if they need to change lanes or swerve. Pass promptly and avoid lingering next to large commercial vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, how should your speed compare to freeway traffic?
options: a:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,b:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,c:At the legal speed limit.
note: Use the freeway entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic already on the freeway. Entering much slower than other vehicles can cause drivers behind you to brake or swerve, creating a hazard. Adjust your speed to merge smoothly with the flow, as long as it is within the legal limit and safe for conditions.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road (such as during hydroplaning), gently ease your foot off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or make sudden turns, because that can cause a skid. As your tires slow slightly, they will regain traction and you can then adjust speed and direction safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If many vehicles are passing you on the right while you are driving in the left lane and the driver behind you wants to go faster, what should you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane when it is safe.,b:Stay in your lane so you don't impede the flow of traffic.,c:Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.
note: The left lane is generally for passing or faster-moving traffic. If vehicles are passing you on the right and a driver behind you wants to go faster, you are likely impeding traffic. When it is safe, move into the right lane so faster vehicles can pass on the left and traffic can flow smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should enter:
options: a:Any available lane.,b:The second lane from the curb.,c:The first (closest) lane on the one-way street.,d:The farthest lane from the curb.
note: When turning from a two-way onto a one-way street, turn into the nearest (first) legal lane of the one-way street.

question: Regulatory signs generally are which of the following?
options: a:White,b:Green,c:Yellow
note: Regulatory signs tell you about laws you must obey, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. In the U.S., these signs are generally white rectangles or squares with black, red, or sometimes green letters or symbols, so white is the correct color choice.

question: Before backing a vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Both walk around the vehicle and look to the front, sides, and rear.,b:Walk completely around the vehicle to be sure no person or obstacle is behind it.,c:Look to the front, sides, and rear.
note: Before backing, you should walk around the vehicle if possible to check for children, pedestrians, or objects that are low and hard to see. Then, get in, check the front, sides, and rear, and continue looking over your shoulder while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors, because they do not show the full blind area behind the vehicle.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins skidding to the left, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,b:Not turn your steering wheel.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: In a skid, always steer in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding. If the rear moves left, you turn the steering wheel left; if it moves right, you turn right. At the same time, ease off the accelerator and avoid hard braking so the tires can regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using your side mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using the inside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; there are blind spots along the sides. To check a blind spot before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Use mirrors first, then a shoulder check, and only change lanes when it is clear.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is in poor condition, what can it cause?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Your suspension system helps keep the tires in contact with the road and stabilizes the vehicle. If it is worn or damaged, the car can bounce, sway, or handle poorly, which can make it harder to steer and control, especially in turns or during sudden maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter a roadway, what should you do regarding the sidewalk?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.,c:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
note: When exiting an alley or driveway, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk or sidewalk area. This allows you to check carefully for pedestrians and other traffic, who have the right‑of‑way. Only after ensuring the sidewalk is clear and it is safe may you proceed.

question: Why should high beam headlights not be used in fog or mist?
options: a:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,b:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.,c:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,d:High beams are illegal in foggy conditions.
note: In fog or mist, high beams shine more light into the tiny water droplets in the air. That light reflects back toward your eyes, creating glare and making it harder to see. Use low beam headlights in fog so the light aims down at the road and improves visibility.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Traffic light ahead.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited in your direction of travel. You must stay in your lane and not cross the line to pass another vehicle, because sight distance or other conditions make passing unsafe.

question: When driving in work zones, what is a safe practice?
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: In work zones, traffic can stop or change lanes suddenly due to workers, equipment, or lane shifts. Keeping a larger following distance and avoiding tailgating gives you more time and space to react safely to unexpected slowdowns or obstacles.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway compared to a city street?
options: a:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:In order to see potential hazards early.
note: At freeway speeds, you cover distance much faster, so hazards can develop quickly. Looking farther ahead lets you spot slow traffic, lane changes, and other problems early, giving you more time to adjust your speed or lane smoothly and safely.

question: Motorcycles on the road are entitled to what lane width?
options: a:The width of the sidewalk.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:One-half of the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as any other motor vehicle. Drivers of cars and trucks should not crowd or share a lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle, because motorcycles need room to maneuver and maintain a safety cushion.

question: How can you check vehicles that are in your blind spots?
options: a:Look over your shoulders.,b:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only use the outside rearview mirrors.,d:Trust the sensors to detect them.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots, in addition to using your mirrors.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow when visibility is poor, you should:
options: a:Turn on your parking lights.,b:Increase instrument panel lighting only.,c:Turn on your headlights (low beams).,d:Use high beam headlights for better visibility.
note: When visibility is poor at dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights. Low beams help you see and be seen without causing glare for other drivers, and many states require headlights whenever wipers are in use.

question: Which statement best describes backing your vehicle?
options: a:Backing up is only dangerous in large vehicles.,b:Backing is safer than driving forward.,c:Backing up is only dangerous if you have a helper.,d:Backing up is always hazardous and requires extra caution.
note: Backing is always more hazardous than driving forward because your view to the rear is limited and it is harder to judge distance and path. Back up slowly, check around your vehicle, use mirrors and cameras if available, and use a spotter when possible.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection allows you to do what?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Adjust your mirrors before entering the intersection.,c:Proceed straight or turn, if the way is clear, at a safe and reasonable speed while yielding to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection or lawfully within the intersection on a conflicting movement.

question: If dust or smoke reduce visibility, what lights should you use?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers only.,d:Hazard lights without headlights.
note: Use your regular headlights (low beams) whenever dust, smoke, fog, or similar conditions reduce visibility. Headlights help you see the road and, just as importantly, help other drivers see you. Parking lights or hazard flashers alone are not sufficient or appropriate for driving in low-visibility conditions.

question: While in a vehicle on a highway, is it legal to have or drink from an open container of alcohol?
options: a:It is illegal to either drink from or possess open containers of alcohol.,b:It is legal to drink alcohol if you're not driving.,c:It is legal to drink alcohol if you're driving but not drunk.
note: Open container laws generally make it illegal for anyone in a moving vehicle on a public road to possess or drink from an open container of alcohol, whether they are the driver or a passenger. Even if you are not driving, you may not legally drink from or have an open alcoholic beverage in the vehicle while it is being operated on the highway.

question: If you see a pedestrian crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.,b:Honk to urge them to hurry.,c:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,d:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
note: Even without a marked crosswalk, you must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and allow them to finish crossing.

question: What does a pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Regulatory sign.,c:School zone or school crossing sign.
note: A pentagon-shaped sign is used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this five-sided sign, be prepared to slow down, watch carefully for children, and obey any posted school zone speed limits or crossing guard directions.

question: When using windshield wipers in rain, snow, or sleet, what else must you do?
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Honk intermittently to alert other drivers to the lowered visibility.
note: When rain, snow, or sleet requires you to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights. This improves your visibility and makes your vehicle easier for others to see. High beams should not be used in precipitation because they can reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

question: How should you behave when you approach a person crossing the street using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the person is safely clear of your path.,b:Honk to let them know you're there and proceed slowly.,c:Carefully drive around them without stopping.,d:Wave them on to cross quickly.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog always have the right‑of‑way. You must stop and remain stopped until they have completely crossed and are well clear of your path, and you should not honk, wave, or try to direct them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers are required to obey instructions from which of the following persons at construction sites?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,d:All of the above.
note: In construction and work zones, drivers must obey the instructions of flaggers (signal persons) and any posted temporary traffic control devices. Flaggers have the same authority as signs or signals, and their directions override normal right‑of‑way rules to keep workers and drivers safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic and pedestrians that are close enough to create a hazard, stopping if necessary.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Slow down but never stop.,d:Proceed first if you signal your intention.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right‑of‑way to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard. If traffic is clear, you may proceed without stopping; if not, you must stop and wait until it is safe.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drink a caffeinated beverage and continue driving.,b:Turn off the radio to concentrate.,c:Open a window and keep driving.,d:Stop and rest or change drivers.
note: Drowsy driving is extremely dangerous. If you feel sleepy, the only safe choice is to get off the road and rest or switch drivers. Tricks like opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking caffeine do not reliably restore alertness and should not be relied on while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you tell you have enough space to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car directly beside you.,b:If the other driver flashes their headlights for you to re-enter the lane.,c:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,d:If you have been in the opposing lane for at least three seconds.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you are safely ahead of the other vehicle. A good rule is to wait until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror; this indicates you have enough space to return without cutting them off.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning in rain, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Put on cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to reduce this risk is to slow down in wet conditions and drive smoothly. Avoid sudden steering or braking, and make sure your tires are properly inflated and have good tread.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection means you must:
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign (stop, yield, then go).,b:Expect the light to turn green shortly.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,d:Treat it only as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Why is night driving more challenging?
options: a:The speed limit is increased at night.,b:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.,c:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.
note: At night, your visibility is limited to the area lit by your headlights, which makes it harder to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving. Because of this, you should reduce speed and make sure you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Construction and maintenance warnings.,b:General warning signs.,c:Regulatory instructions like speed limits.,d:Guide signs for motorists.
note: Orange traffic signs are used in work zones. They warn drivers about construction, maintenance, and temporary traffic control changes so you can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any posted instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you frequently pass other cars on a two-lane road by speeding, what is the likely result?
options: a:You will arrive more quickly and more safely.,b:You will minimize your risk of an accident.,c:You will help reduce traffic congestion.,d:You will increase your chances of a collision.
note: Frequently passing on a two-lane road usually means driving faster than surrounding traffic and spending more time in the oncoming lane. This greatly increases your risk of a head-on or side collision. Safe driving means keeping a steady, legal speed and passing only when it is legal, necessary, and clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.,c:You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: When you have a green light, you may go only if the intersection is clear. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk or entering on a proper signal have the right-of-way. You must wait until they have safely crossed your lane before proceeding, even if your light is green.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers when they want to slow down.
note: Large trucks are heavy and need a much longer distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver room to brake and helps prevent rear-end collisions if traffic slows or stops suddenly.

question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on a layer of water. How can you help prevent it?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of water. The faster you drive on wet roads, the more likely this is to happen. Slowing down and driving smoothly in the rain greatly reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:Loading zone.,b:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red-painted curb means you may not stop, stand, or park there at any time, except when required to obey a traffic signal or officer. It is used where stopping would create a serious safety hazard or block emergency access.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no-passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: If another driver is passing you illegally in a no-passing zone, do not speed up or compete for the lane. Instead, slow down slightly and keep to the right as needed so the passing driver can return to the proper lane as quickly and safely as possible.

question: When a school bus is stopped to pick up or drop off children, what must motorists do?
options: a:Stop as required by law when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Stop only if you are driving in the same direction on any road, including divided highways.
note: You must stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. However, on a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median, oncoming traffic in the opposite direction is usually not required to stop (they should proceed with caution). Always know your state’s specific rules, but in most cases you stop when traveling in the same direction and when on an undivided roadway in either direction.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Left, toward the center of the road,b:Straight ahead,c:Right, toward the side of the road
note: When parking downhill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the side of the road. If the vehicle rolls, it will move away from traffic instead of into the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped at a red light but a green arrow points your direction, when may you proceed?
options: a:You may proceed if you are in the proper lane, the intersection is clear, and you yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.,b:You must first come to a complete stop, then proceed.,c:You must wait until the circular red light changes.
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, after yielding to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection. You do not need to stop first unless required by a sign or traffic condition.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.,b:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,c:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop.
note: In work zones, reduce your speed, obey all posted work zone signs, and be prepared to stop suddenly. Workers, equipment, and lane shifts can appear unexpectedly, so extra caution is required.

question: What message is displayed on a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:One-way.,c:Stop.
note: A red octagon-shaped sign always means STOP. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: To minimize glare from the headlights of an oncoming car, what should you do?
options: a:Close one eye until the car passes.,b:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,c:Flash your high beams back to the other driver.,d:Keep your focus on the centerline of the road.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide, while still checking the road ahead with your peripheral vision. Avoid staring directly into the oncoming lights, which can temporarily blind you.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:Just after it starts to rain.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Roads are often most slippery just after it starts to rain because the water lifts oil, grease, and other residues to the surface, creating a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this buildup is washed away and traction usually improves, though you should still drive carefully.

question: Do sudden wind gusts on highways affect only large vehicles?
options: a:No — they can affect all vehicles and cause problems.,b:Yes — only large vehicles are affected.,c:They only cause visibility issues, not handling problems.,d:They only affect motorcycles.
note: Sudden wind gusts can affect the steering and stability of any vehicle, not just large trucks or buses. Lighter vehicles and motorcycles can be pushed sideways, and even passenger cars may drift in their lane. Always keep a firm grip on the wheel and be prepared to adjust your steering in strong winds.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice or snow often causes what problem?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: On ice or snow, hard continuous braking can cause the wheels to lock, which makes you lose steering control and can lead to a skid. Instead, slow down early and brake gently and gradually. If your vehicle does not have ABS, use a light, pumping action on the brakes to help maintain control.

question: When must a vehicle be covered by liability insurance?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only when used on public roads.,c:Only when operated by a minor.
note: Liability insurance is required whenever a motor vehicle is operated on public roads. It helps pay for injuries or property damage you may cause to others in a crash. You must maintain this coverage at all times the vehicle is driven or parked on public streets or highways.

question: When driving in fog, you should use which type of headlights?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off water droplets in fog, rain, or snow and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Never drive with just parking lights in these conditions.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Because large vehicles have priority on the road.,b:Because large vehicles always travel faster than small ones.,c:Because small vehicles cannot see large vehicles in their rearview mirrors.,d:Because larger vehicles need longer distances to stop and may not be able to avoid a collision.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop. If you brake suddenly in front of them, the driver may not be able to stop in time, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision. Always avoid cutting closely in front of large vehicles and leave extra space.

question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?
options: a:Ensure the lane is clear before moving over.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Check mirrors for approaching vehicles.,d:Change lanes abruptly or without signaling.
note: You should never change lanes abruptly or without signaling. Safe lane changes require signaling in advance, checking your mirrors, and looking over your shoulder to check blind spots. This gives other drivers time to react and helps prevent sideswipe and rear-end collisions.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle when which condition is met?
options: a:You may never cross any double yellow lines to pass another vehicle.,b:You may cross when the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:You may cross when the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.,d:You may cross double solid yellow lines if no traffic is coming.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may cross it to pass when it is safe and legal. If the yellow line next to your lane is solid, you may not pass, even if the line on the other side is broken. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing for traffic in either direction.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,b:Continue ahead because the motorist has the right-of-way.,c:Slow down or stop and wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing the street.,d:Honk your horn to warn the pedestrians to hurry across.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Slow down or stop and wait until pedestrians have completely crossed your lane before proceeding. Going around pedestrians or assuming you have the right-of-way is dangerous and illegal.

question: Under Alabama law, when must headlights be used?
options: a:Only between midnight and 5 AM,b:From sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is less than 500 feet,c:Only when it is raining or snowing,d:Only on rural roads without streetlights
note: Alabama requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and any time weather or road conditions reduce visibility to less than 500 feet. This includes rain, fog, and dust. Many states also require headlights whenever wipers are in use — always check local rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a pentagon (five-sided) shaped sign indicate in Alabama?
options: a:A state highway route marker,b:A school zone or school crossing ahead,c:A yield condition at a merge,d:An agricultural or farm zone
note: A pentagon-shaped sign (pointing downward, like an arrowhead) is used exclusively for school zone and school crossing warnings in the United States. This distinctive shape makes school zone signs immediately recognizable even at a distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on an undivided Alabama road and a funeral procession is passing from the opposite direction. What should you do?
options: a:Maintain normal speed — funeral processions have no special right of way,b:Pull to the right and stop until the procession has passed,c:Proceed normally but do not enter the procession,d:Flash your headlights to signal respect
note: Alabama law requires drivers to yield to funeral processions — pull to the right and stop until the procession has completely passed. Funeral processions have right-of-way at intersections. Cutting into or through a procession is both illegal and disrespectful.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection in Alabama where two vehicles arrive at the same time from different directions, who has the right of way?
options: a:The vehicle traveling on the larger road,b:The vehicle that flashes headlights first,c:The vehicle on the RIGHT has the right of way over the vehicle on the LEFT,d:The vehicle going straight has priority over turning vehicles
note: At an uncontrolled intersection when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the RIGHT has the right of way. The driver on the left must yield. This basic right-of-way rule applies at 4-way stops, intersections without signs, and anywhere two vehicles arrive at the same time.

question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the statutory speed limit on unpaved roads in Alabama?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:45 mph
note: Under Alabama statutory speed laws, the default speed limit on unpaved roads is 35 miles per hour, unless another limit is posted.
